text:
Steve (Acme): Hey, we're seeing streaming responses cut off mid-token then client reconnects immediately and we get duplicated tokens/billing for the same logical request. Happened ~3x in last hour. request id: req_8b3a. Anyone seen this pattern?

support-jen: Sorry you're hitting this — looking now. Are you using our JS SDK or raw SSE from your backend? Any sample request you can paste?

Steve (Acme): Raw SSE from a Node backend. Simple repro: server opens stream, sometimes client sees silence for ~15s then connection closes, client retries immediate. curl works but flaky.

alex: tagging @eng-runtime — this smells like the ALB/edge idle timeout vs our comment-ping cadence mismatch. Could also be Cloudflare + long-polling.

eng-runtime-tom: Steve, can you attach server logs for req_8b3a and say what sits in front of you (ALB/nginx/GCLB)? Also confirm client reconnect backoff behaviour.

sre-bot: Log snippet for req_8b3a: 
```
[2026-03-12T14:07:02Z] conn=abcd1234 read=0s silence=15s -> closed by peer
[2026-03-12T14:07:02Z] inference=req_8b3a aborted mid-stream
```
No 502/504 seen at edge. TCP state shows FIN from client.

maria: We recently debugged a "ghost connection" where the proxy thought the TCP session was alive but the client process had crashed and the kernel emitted FIN later. Our comment-ping (":ping

") approach relies on clients honoring the SSE colon-comment; some proxies drop it or strip out idle events. Suggest enabling OS-level TCP keepalive (interval ~60s) on client side and also emitting an explicit SSE keepalive every 10s from the server: `:keepalive

`.

eng-runtime-tom: Another angle — if client reconnects without Last-Event-ID, server treats it as a fresh generation and billing shows a new token stream. We have a short dedupe window for very quick retries (5s) if client sends Last-Event-ID. If client retries immediately with no resume header, we re-run the model.

Steve (Acme): That explains the billing spikes. Is there an API-level recommended pattern to resume so we don't double-charge?

support-jen: Best practice: client should include Last-Event-ID header when reconnecting (we accept `Last-Event-ID` for SSE resume), implement exponential backoff with jitter for retries, and prefer draining/killing the old event stream gracefully. We'll also recommend a client-side TCP keepalive.

alex: For customers behind ALBs, idle timeout defaults can be 60s. If comment pings are >60s, ALB closes. Also some managed proxies remove colon-comments. In those cases TCP keepalive is more reliable.

maria: Quick repro script you can try to see the disconnect deterministically: 
```bash
TOKEN=xxx
curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -N "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream" | sed -n '1,40p'
```
If you see silence but TCP still open, run `tcpdump -w trace.pcap port 443 and host api.redwood.example` and share.

eng-runtime-tom: Action items from eng-runtime: 1) Add server-side config to emit comment pings from edge for customers who opt-in; 2) Extend dedupe window for very short burst retries to reduce double billing; 3) Add telemetry alert for `reconnects -> new-generation` spikes. I'll file a follow-up and link here.

maria: Temporary mitigation for Steve: enable client TCP keepalive (60s), add Last-Event-ID on reconnects, and add jittered backoff (e.g., 100ms * 2^n with max 5s). That should prevent immediate duplicate generations.

Steve (Acme): OK we'll try those changes and run the curl/tcpdump repro. Will post logs/pcap if it reproduces. Thanks. :thumbsup:

support-jen: Thanks, please paste results. If you can attach pcap + trace we'll escalate to runtime team for immediate patch. :eyes:

eng-runtime-tom: opened ticket INF-2147 to track server-side ping flag + dedupe window. Assigning to runtime sprint.

Steve (Acme): One follow-up — is there a way to see in billing logs that two charges are from retries vs legitimate two runs? The UI currently just shows tokens per request id and sometimes new request ids.

support-jen: We can correlate using `client_id` and `last_event_id` if present; we'll pull logs for req_8b3a and return a correlation. If you prefer, we can also do a temporary credit for duplicates while we investigate.

Steve (Acme): Appreciate that — will send the pcap and the curl output.

alex: Noting for the runbook: prefer TCP keepalive + Last-Event-ID resume + exponential backoff. We'll update the support KB with a short checklist.

maria: I'll also add a note about proxies that strip colon-comments — that was key in another customer's case.

support-jen: Closing loop: we have a repro path, mitigations, and an eng ticket. Leaving thread open until you confirm.

Steve (Acme): Will confirm after tests. Thanks everyone.
